utterances.text: Could you now tell me, sir, whether at one point in time your wife and daughter left Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second thing I did was to send them off in the direction of Serbia, to be more precise, in the direction of Krusevac as I had a brother who lived in Krusevac with his family, and I hoped that he would put them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And tell me, did you at some point in time return to Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even leave Bosnia and Herzegovina. I only escorted my wife and daughter, and then as it was clear to me that I had to become engaged, I sought out part of the special unit that I had previously worked in, and I joined the educational centre of the MUP in the Sarajevo settlement of Vraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me, after that were you assigned a position of some kind in that unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was still in my tracksuit and in training shoes, but I was assigned as a -- an operative duty commander in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did that unit remain in Vraca in the subsequent period after you had returned?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, towards the end of May we were moved -- or rather, we moved the command of the special unit to Brdo, to a hill above Vraca. It was at the top. It was Moravska Street, perhaps, and our lines were -- or positions stretched along the hill that is called the Hrasno Hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, afterwards did the unit move somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the 6th or 7th of June, because the people were exhausted, we withdrew the unit to rest in the premises of the Sarajevo factory Envergoinvest, which is located in the Lukavica settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And then did you get some other position with your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men briefly stayed in the presence of the Envergoinvest factory, and then some were selected to rest in the Jahorina Moharina [phoen], in the Kosuta Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. If you can remember, do you remember whether the unit then moved to some other place? Did it have its headquarters somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left Jahorina to perform tasks in the Sarajevo settlement of Vraca. And then I, in fact, towards the end of July - I can't remember the exact date - was granted a brief leave to visit my family. They were staying with my brother in Krusevac, my son and daughter and my entire family, in fact, was there. I stayed there for four or five days. When I returned, when I moved from Serbia into Bosnia and Herzegovina or to Zvornik, to be more precise, I met members of my special unit at checkpoints in the direction of Sekovici. I was surprised. I asked what they were doing there. They told me they had been there for three or four days already. Later, I found out they had been assigned a task, the task of neutralizing some paramilitary formation in Zvornik known as Zuta Osa or the Yellow Wasp. I know that the mission was accomplished successfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, did the headquarters of the unit remain there for a while, or was the location changed, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having accomplished the mission and having neutralized the paramilitary formations, the unit was provided with accomodation in the Drina hotel in Zvornik, and then some were selected to move from Jahorina to Zvornik. But part of the unit, a small part of the unit remained on Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me, how much time did the unit stay in Zvornik? How long did it stay there, and did it then move to some other location?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed in the Drina hotel in Zvornik until the winter of 1993, 1994, up until February or March. That's when changes were introduced in the brigade command; the structure of the command was changed. The head of the brigade was changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where did the brigade -- where did the unit move from Zvornik, and then I'll continue with other questions.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early spring, in February or March, 1994, the unit was moved the Janja settlement, to the premises where we already had a police detachment of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now tell me, as far as you can remember, when was the special police brigade established? That's what it was called, later became the special police brigade. When did this happen? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was involved in those tasks, and I think that when the special police brigade was formed -- well, I think they had already started forming it in the autumn of 1992. I think it was in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, now, during this period of time that we have been discussing, what sort of duties did you have to perform in the unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, initially I had the following tasks in Zvornik. I had to deal with personnel issues, all personnel issues that related to the unit. I took care of seriously -- of the seriously wounded, of the families of those who had been seriously wounded or killed. I also dealt with administrative issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in 1995, where were the brigade headquarters located?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same place where we were moved to in 1994, in Janja.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you now tell me, to the best of your recollection, what was the structure of the command of the special police brigade in 1995? What was the command structure like?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the head of the brigade, there was the commander, Goran Saric; the deputy commander, Ljubomir Borovcanin; the assistant commander for logistics, Milutin Ratkovic; the assistant for training, Dusko Jevic; the assistant for personnel affairs, Obrad Savic; the assistant for logistics support, Vitomir Kapuran and so on. At that time, I had a decision according to which I was an official for information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like to put a few questions to you that have to do with the special police brigade, and it relates to 1995, the year 1995. Do you remember whether at the time in 1995 there were any ranks in the police, and were there any ranks in the special police brigade as well?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in the second half of 1995, something was done to assign ranks, and ranks actually came to life or started being used on the 21st of November, let's say, 21st of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would like to move on to a different subject. It concerns the training centre in Jahorina and the police forces staffs. Tell me, do you remember when the police forces staff was established on Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was February or March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, tell me, what was the reason for establishing this staff on Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reason for establishing the staff was to obtain operative information for the police services; and on the other hand, from the direction of Sarajevo we wanted to prepare for a spring offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to have a look at a number of documents that have to do with the police forces staff on Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first one I would like to have a look at is 4D622.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You'll see it on the screen. Unfortunately, we don't have a translation, so I'll go through it with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just show the entire document on the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- so that you can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we can enlarge it a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the first page. It's a dispatch from the command of the special police brigade, Goran Saric. It's dated the 15th of March, 1995. In this document, he informs a number of levels in the MUP, in a number of departments about the activities taken to establish a staff for the police forces. And now let's have a look at the first paragraph in the document. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the basis of a written order from the deputy minister of internal affairs and the leader of the RJB on establishing police forces staff for the needs of control and command in the upcoming combat operations on the Sarajevo battlefield. "In addition to the activities mentioned in the dispatch, we have undertaken the following" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, I don't want to go through the entire document, to read through the entire document. I would just like to gain a picture of what is at stake in the document, and therefore, I'd like to have a look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this corresponds to what I actually witnessed on Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And on this page, we see what they say about efficient operations of the staff, how it should achieve efficiency. It mentions the measures that should be taken to make sure that the staff functions properly. Tell me, this document shows that we're dealing with a written order from the deputy of the -- deputy minister of the MUP, a written order on establishing the staff.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is already the implementation of this oral order. It's an oral order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a look at 4D391.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We can go through the document a little more rapidly because we have a translation into English. It's an order from the Ministry of the Interior Zivko Rakic. It is dated the 16th of March, 1995. It is an order on forming a command and control staff of the police forces in the Sarajevo battlefield, and we see the date at the top of the document, the 16th of March, 1995, and we can see who the addressees are. We have the public security department, the state security department, the police forces staff, and so on and so forth. Have a look at the order. Who, according to this order, should become part of the staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a number of segments of the police, of special police units, logistics material and financial assistance. All I can do is confirm that this was implemented. I witnessed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And according to this order, who was designated as the commander of the staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here it says Saric, Goran.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at item 5 of the order where it says that "Continuous functioning of the staff should be issued as of the 20th of March."

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 20th of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to bear in mind the break between the question and the answer. Please wait a little before you start giving your answer, and I'll try to bear in mind the same. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's now move to the following document, which is 4D -- I apologise. [In English] [previous translation continues]... to page 65, line 15. It should read: "The 20th of March." This is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seemed that this hasn't been recorded. In any case, the document that I wanted to show you next is 4D623. Very well. If we look at the document now, we will see that this is information by Dusko Jevic, the command of the special police brigade, and the date is 28th of March, 1995. And we see that he informs the command of the special police brigade about the concrete steps that were taken with a view to establishing the staff. I would like to show you, first of all, the written version of this version -- the handwritten version for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is the same. Can we please look at page -- at the following page. Let's just look at the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we look at this document, in handwriting the number is 1/95, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. According to your best knowledge, what was the reason for the establishment of the education and training centre of the Ministry of the Interior Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning of the war, we trained police officers for simple tasks in the police; and three years into the war, because of the casualties, people being wounded, there was a constant shortage of men, so the units were replenished with military conscripts who had not undergone police training. That is why periodically police training courses were organised for police apprentices to provide them with the necessary skills and knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the centre for training of the Republika Srpska MUP, did you have a position, a function? Did you have to do anything with the staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was in charge of the logistics support. The offices had to be equipped. Office supplies had to be provided with basic -- basic equipment had to be procured, and that's what was happening at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One more thing I would like to ask you. According to your best recollection, did Mr. Borovcanin have a position? Did he have a function to perform at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the following document. This is 4D400.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Since we have it in front of us, on the right-hand side is the document in Serbian. Again, this is a report of the police forces commander Jahorina Trnovo, Dusko Jevic. The date of 1st of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the number this document bears in the right-hand side corner. The number is 3/92, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the commander of the Jahorina Trnovo police forces informs the Ministry of the Interior that the trainees started arriving at the Jahorina Hotel. We can see this in the first paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Further on, we can see that the commander of the police staff forces is requesting that officers who have been selected for command and control should be sent -- sent urgently to prevent any possible problems.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now that we have seen the document and we have seen the list of addressees - which is the public security department, the police administration, the special police brigade - what training course is referred to in this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this training course was organised for members of our detachments who had not been trained despite the fact that they were still involved in combat. However, they had not undergone previous police training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was that a course for policemen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And it arises from this document that there is a possible problem with officers who were supposed to be in charge of the training course. Could you please tell me, which officers were supposed to manage the course? Who were the lecturers? Where were they supposed to arrive from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were teachers, i.e., professors from the school of the interior who were trained to educate future policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were there also lecturers from the special brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for special physical training they could be instructors, for special training, the use of chemicals and similar things. And the theory of policing was something that was lectured by full-time professors. They were the only ones with the degree that enabled them to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm just waiting for the -- for your answer to be recorded properly. Tell me, please, according to the best of your recollection, did the course take off the ground in that period?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that they -- those courses were organised periodically, even before. So I am fully convinced that the training courses continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally participate in the training?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I would like us to look at the following document, which is 4D251. I would kindly ask the Court to produce the document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a dispatch by the Jahorina commander. The number is 5/95, and the date is 6 April 1995. The dispatch was sent to a number of addresses in the MUP of Republika Srpska. Could we please look at the second page to inspect the signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the second page, please. Can the next page be produced in e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Again, the dispatch was sent from the police forces command Jahorina Trnovo, and it was co-signed by Dusko Jevic and Cedo Tosic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the people, and I can confirm the credibility of the signatures. I worked with both of them for a number of years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to the first page in order to remove an ambiguity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, it says: "In the evening of 5 February 1995, a group of trainees arrived from the CJB Zvornik (8 trainees) so that the total number of trainees now is 142." In view of the date when this dispatch was sent and the date that is mentioned herein as the date of the arrival of the trainees from Zvornik, is this really the 5th of February, 1995, or is this a typo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a typo, obviously. It should be the 6th of April, and the information applies to that course. It's obvious that it was very difficult to set up a course of that nature and to implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, if we look at what we have already read in the first paragraph of this document, does the number of 142 trainees tell you something about the implementation of this training course?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that those were members of the special police brigade and public security centres. A reference is made here to eight trainees from Zvornik, but I'm sure that there were others from other public security centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the bottom part of the document where it says "It has been agreed with the deputy commander of the special police brigade," and here a reference made to a certain number of names: Nedo Sevo on behalf of the school of internal affairs, and Aco Milic, a psychologist from the school. What does this tell us about the lecturers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the lecturers were full-time professors from the school of the -- of internal affairs and that special police training was carried out by the instructors from our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move on to the next document, which is 4D252.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a dispatch by the commander of the staff of the police forces Jahorina Trnovo, Dusko Jevic. The number is 11/95, and the date is 8 April 1995. We see that this is a request to send Tomo Mirosavic to work with the trainees. Do you know where Tomo Mirosavic came from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was the Chief of Staff of a department at the school of internal affairs; in any case, he was a full-time professor. It's obvious that a lecture was missing for one of the modules of the course, and it the commander believes that Tomo Mirosavic would be the best-suited person to fill the position. I wouldn't be able to tell you what his specialty was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now, can you remember modules of the course? What kind of training was provided to the trainees during the course?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very special -- a very simple training course for beginners. The trainees were informed about the law on internal affairs. They were familiarized with policing procedures, patrolling, and they were provided some special physical training. They were familiarized with weapons, chemical agents and similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, could you please tell me if you remember, how long did the course last?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as a rule the courses would normally last three weeks, about 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know on the base of what a programme was this course the policemen conducted?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, usually there was a -- an officer who would prepare for the main courses. He'd assess the conditions and take into consideration the time-period concerned. But it varied. It was on the basis of experience and varied from course to course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's now have a look at the following document. Unfortunately, we don't have a translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4D624 is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'll just put a few questions to you about this document, since it's one you have already seen. Could we just have a look at it? Can you tell us what the title of the document is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republika Srpska, the ministry of internal affairs, special police brigade, police force staff, Jahorina Trnovo." That's the title -- or rather, the title is "The programme for professional training for the police course." I'm familiar with this handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's not very clear here. Perhaps we could scroll down a bit to see the date.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the very same course. The date is the 10th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, you said that you recognized the handwriting. Whose handwriting is this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Dusko Jevic's handwriting, the deputy commander of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already seen this document. Can you just tell us something about the contents of the document, especially with regard to the programme for professional training?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the programme consists of various subjects that have to be dealt with during the course and on a day-by-day basis. You start off on Monday. Then you have Tuesday, Wednesday. The subjects change. Some of the subjects can be modified, can be changed. If there is inclement weather, one subject can be taught instead of another. But on the whole, it's physical preparation, training, shooting, and learning about chemical agents, et cetera. I've already mentioned this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like to put a few more questions to you before we adjourn for the day. Do you remember, perhaps, that at one point in time some of the beginners at the police course were moved to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that. I don't understand why this was done. Perhaps it was to bring some unit up to strength in order to secure a road - at the time, Konjevic Polje was a checkpoint -- or there was a checkpoint in Konjevic Polje; there wasn't combat of any kind - or perhaps to gain experience in the course -- of the course itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let's just have a look at the following document, 4D625.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a dispatch dated the 11th of April, 1995. And if we have a look at the signature at the bottom, it says the commander of the 8th special police detachment, Branislav Okuka. And if we have a look at the first paragraph of the document, it says, "Having visited the course attendees who are presently in Konjevic Polje, it has been established that the following attendees joined the course later..." and then you have the names of the individuals concerned. Can you tell me whether this document, and in relation to what we have just discussed, in relation to sending some of the beginners to Konjevic Polje, has it got anything to do with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume that this commander was working on behalf one of the -- was working as one of the officers on the course, perhaps a company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... maybe we can adjourn just right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Witness, we are going to stop here today. We will continue tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15. Between now and tomorrow, it's important that you do not communicate or you let anyone communicate with you on the subject matter of your testimony. It's an obligation that you have. Have you understood me? All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of October, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.57 p.m.,
